# ShellAge: a curated database of shell growth rings and lifespan in bivalves

**Authors:** Ada Example^1,\*^, Ben Sample^2^

## Abstract

Shell growth rings record the age of a bivalve, and earlier compilations of bivalve lifespans mixed ring counts
with guesses. ShellAge re-reads every ring count from the original sources and records each change with its cause.
It holds 412 species, 160 of them new, with lifespans from ring counts in 389 of them. Most correlations between
shell thickness and lifespan that pass the false discovery rate fail on phylogenetically independent contrasts:
14 of 52 keep their sign and significance.

> AUTHOR: trim to 150 words once the journal is chosen.

## Introduction

Bivalves include the longest-lived animals known. Earlier compilations of their lifespans were assembled by hand
and never re-checked.

## Results

### Database content

ShellAge holds 412 species from 61 families. In the sampled families, thicker shells were associated with longer
lifespans before the contrasts were applied. Most correlations between shell thickness and lifespan that pass the
false discovery rate fail on phylogenetically independent contrasts.
